name: email-draft-from-brief
aliases: turn key points into an email
summary: Drafts an email from a short brief in the specialist's own voice, producing a subject line, body, and alternate subject options. Reach for it when you have a purpose, recipient, and key points but no drafted email yet, and you want a ready-to-review first draft. It applies your installed communication style profile from [[communication-style-profile]] if one exists, or a plain, direct, professional voice when none is installed. The draft is yours to review and send; Copilot never sends.
use_cases: You have a purpose, recipient, and key points but no drafted email yet.; You want to turn purpose, recipient, key points, and target tone into a ready-to-review draft.; You want the email written in your own first-person voice using your style profile from [[communication-style-profile]].; You want two alternate subject line options to choose from.; You need a fast first draft that a person reviews before it is sent.
expected_outputs: Subject plus body draft; Alternate subject line options; Note on which style profile was applied, if any
prompt_text:
Run this in Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat to produce the file output specified at the end. If you are running in Copilot in Outlook instead, return only the subject line and body into the compose window and skip the file output contract.

You should have these inputs: (1) purpose, (2) recipient and whether they are internal or external, (3) key points, (4) target tone. If any input is missing or unreadable, stop and list what is missing. Never proceed from memory or invent content for a missing input.

Your single task: draft an email from a short brief.

Method:
1. Read the purpose, recipient, key points, and target tone I provide below, and my installed communication style profile if one is available to you in Custom Instructions or Memory; if none is available, use a plain, direct, professional voice and note that no style profile was applied.
2. Draft a subject line and body that accomplishes the stated purpose, covers every key point, and matches the target tone and my style profile.
3. Propose two alternate subject lines.
4. State which style profile, if any, you applied.
5. Do not add a commitment, deadline, or promise not present in the key points I gave you.

Write the email in my first-person voice; it is my email, not Copilot's, and the body never references AI assistance.

Source of truth: the purpose, recipient, key points, and tone I provide are the only sources for content; do not invent facts, dates, or commitments.

This is a draft for my review before sending, not a sent email. Do not represent it as final or already sent. Do not fabricate a fact, name, or commitment not present in the inputs I provide.

name: email-reply-with-regulatory-position
aliases: answer whether a claim is allowed
state a compliance position in email
summary: Drafts a reply that states a regulatory position with citations, holding or escalating rather than committing the company to a position it cannot fully substantiate. Reach for it when an incoming email or thread asks you to state or confirm a regulatory position, such as whether a claim is allowed or whether a label change is compliant. It states the position clearly in your first-person voice, cites the exact provisions it rests on, marks every citation UNVERIFIED until you confirm it against the current eCFR, and adds a hold or escalation note (with a named review gate for external recipients or novel or contested positions).
use_cases: An incoming email or thread asks whether a specific claim is allowed under FDA rules.; Someone asks you to confirm that a proposed label change is compliant.; You have a position and its supporting citations and need them turned into a clear reply a non-specialist can follow.; Your position does not fully resolve the question and you need the reply to hold or escalate rather than overstate certainty.; The recipient is external, or the position is novel or contested, and the reply must name a review gate (regulatory counsel or your manager) before it can be sent.
expected_outputs: Reply stating the position, in the specialist's first-person voice; Citations list, each marked UNVERIFIED pending the specialist's confirmation against the current eCFR; Hold or escalation note, including a named review gate (regulatory counsel or manager) when the recipient is external or the position is novel or contested
prompt_text:
Run this in Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat to produce the file output specified at the end. If you are running in Copilot in Outlook instead, return only the subject line and reply body into the compose window and skip the file output contract.

You should have these inputs: (1) the incoming email or thread, (2) my regulatory position and the citations it rests on, (3) the recipient type (internal or external). If any input is missing or unreadable, stop and list what is missing. Never proceed from memory or invent content for a missing input.

Your single task: draft a reply that states a regulatory position with citations.

Source of truth: the position and citations I provide are what this reply states; the incoming email/thread is what it responds to. Do not state a position stronger than what my supplied position and citations actually support.

Citation discipline: use only the citations I supply. Never invent a provision, subsection, or threshold. Check each supplied citation for form (title, part, section, paragraph, e.g. 21 CFR 101.22(k)) and for apparent fit to the stated position; flag any citation that looks malformed, misdirected, or insufficient in the hold or escalation note. Mark every citation UNVERIFIED in the citations list: I must confirm each one against the current eCFR before sending. Your own knowledge of the CFR is not verification.

Method:
1. Read the incoming email/thread and my stated position and citations below, and identify exactly what regulatory question is being asked.
2. Draft a reply that states the position clearly, in plain language a non-specialist recipient can follow, while citing the exact regulatory provision(s) my position rests on.
3. If my supplied position and citations do not fully resolve the question being asked, do not fill the gap yourself; draft the reply to state what is confirmed, and add an explicit hold or escalation note naming what is still needed (e.g. "confirming with [role] before finalizing").
4. Do not overstate certainty; if a citation's current status cannot be confirmed, say so in the hold or escalation note rather than presenting it as settled.
5. If the recipient is external, or the position is novel or contested, the hold or escalation note must name a review gate: regulatory counsel or my manager signs off before this reply is sent.

Write the reply in my first-person voice: the position is mine as the regulatory labeling specialist, never Copilot's, and the body never references AI assistance. The reply never characterizes itself as legal advice.

This is a draft for my review before sending, not a sent reply. Do not fabricate a citation, a regulatory conclusion, or a commitment beyond what I supplied as my position.

[Paste my position and citations here]

name: email-thread-to-actions
aliases: turn a thread into action items
who owns what from this thread
summary: Converts an email thread into a summary, decisions made, action items with owners, and open regulatory questions, so nothing discussed in email gets lost. Reach for it when a thread has run long enough (or reached a conclusion) that its content needs to become tracked decisions and actions rather than staying buried in email. It reads the thread end to end and extracts what was decided, what still needs doing, and what regulatory questions remain open, attributing each decision and action to the person named in the thread. When any participant is legal counsel, it marks the output privileged and confidential.
use_cases: A thread has run long enough that its content needs to become tracked decisions and actions rather than staying buried in email.; A thread reached a conclusion and you need the decisions and next steps captured before they are lost.; You need every action item pulled out with its owner and any stated due date.; You need the open regulatory questions the thread raised but did not resolve.; The thread includes legal counsel and the summary must be marked privileged and confidential.
expected_outputs: Summary; Decisions, each attributed to the person who made it; Action items with owners; Open questions; Privileged-and-confidential marking when the thread includes legal counsel
prompt_text:
Run this in Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat. Your single task: convert an email thread into a summary, decisions, action items, and open questions.

You should have this input: (1) the full email thread, in chronological order. If the thread is missing, truncated, or unreadable, stop and list what is missing. Never proceed from memory or invent content for a missing input.

Method:
1. Read the entire thread I provide below, in chronological order.
2. Write a short summary of what the thread was about and how it resolved (or where it stands if unresolved).
3. List every decision actually made in the thread; every decision names the person who made it, exactly as stated in the thread; do not infer a decision that was discussed but not actually settled.
4. List every action item mentioned, with an owner (the person named in the thread) and a due date if one was stated; if no owner or date was given, say so rather than assigning one.
5. List every regulatory question raised in the thread that was not resolved by the end of it.
6. If any participant in the thread is legal counsel (internal or external), put the line "PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL - contains attorney communications" directly under the H1, and end the output by telling me to confirm handling with counsel before saving or sharing this file.

Source of truth: the thread I provide is the only source; do not add a decision, owner, or deadline not stated in it.

This is a summarization pass, not a decision-making one; unresolved items stay listed as open questions, never resolved here.

Do not fabricate a decision, an owner, or a deadline not present in the thread.

name: email-tone-and-clarity-revision
summary: Revises an existing email draft for tone, clarity, and commitment risk, flagging any wording that could read as overcommitment or an inadvertent compliance claim. Reach for it when a draft already exists (from [[email-draft-from-brief]] or written directly) and needs a tone and clarity pass before sending. It revises against a target tone, applies your style profile from [[communication-style-profile]] if one is installed (or a plain, direct, professional voice when none is), lists every change made, and flags phrases that overcommit the company or make an inadvertent regulatory or health claim.
use_cases: A draft email exists and needs a tone and clarity pass before sending.; You want the draft revised against a specific target tone and your style profile from [[communication-style-profile]].; You want a line-by-line change list showing what was edited and why.; You want any phrase that overcommits the company on a deadline, outcome, or regulatory position flagged, not silently rewritten.; You want any inadvertent nutrient content, health, or implied "healthy" claim caught before it goes out.

prompt_text:
Run this in Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat to produce the file output specified at the end. If you are running in Copilot in Outlook instead, return only the revised subject line and body into the compose window and skip the file output contract.

You should have these inputs: (1) the draft email, (2) the target tone. If any input is missing or unreadable, stop and list what is missing. Never proceed from memory or invent content for a missing input.

Your single task: revise a draft email for tone, clarity, and commitment risk.

Method:
1. Read the draft email and target tone I provide below, and my installed communication style profile if one is available to you in Custom Instructions or Memory; if none is available, use a plain, direct, professional voice and note that no style profile was applied.
2. Revise for tone (matching the target tone and my style profile) and clarity (shorter sentences, one point per sentence, no ambiguity about who is doing what by when).

This is a draft revision for my review before sending, not a sent email. Do not fabricate a fact or commitment not present in the original draft.
